sourceName: Boondockers Welcome and Harvest Hosts -- policy/program assessment only, no individual host locations
method: Per task instructions, individual Boondockers Welcome and Harvest Hosts host locations require a paid membership login to view exact addresses and were NOT scraped, guessed, or fabricated -- this file intentionally contains zero location records. Researched program mechanics, cost, and public-map/host-count claims via each service's own site and its official help center, plus independent reporting, to write the policyNote below.
policyNote: WHAT THEY ARE: Boondockers Welcome and Harvest Hosts are both paid membership programs (now under common ownership -- Harvest Hosts acquired Boondockers Welcome) connecting travelers with private hosts (farms, wineries, breweries, individual driveways, museums, golf courses, etc.) willing to let self-contained rigs stay one free night. COST: Boondockers Welcome is $79/year for unlimited stays across 2,800+ host locations (boondockerswelcome.com/become-a-guest, retrieved 2026-08-12). Harvest Hosts has three tiers -- Classic $99/yr, Plus Boondockers Welcome $169/yr, All Access $179/yr for 9,500+ combined locations (harvesthosts.com blog 'What Is Harvest Hosts? A Complete Guide', retrieved 2026-08-12). PUBLIC MAP: Harvest Hosts has a 'mostly public' Discover map at harvesthosts.com/discover -- pins are visible and roughly located without an account, but the host's name, exact address, photos, and reviews are hidden until you join; California alone shows 381 Harvest Hosts locations per the site's own state directory page (retrieved 2026-08-12). Boondockers Welcome does not appear to offer an equivalent public preview map -- its host map requires an account. CRITICAL FIT PROBLEM FOR THIS APP: both programs explicitly EXCLUDE the exact use case wattnap serves. Per Harvest Hosts' and Boondockers Welcome's own help-center articles ('What does self-contained mean and why is this a requirement', 'Boondockers Welcome Guest Requirements' -- support.harvesthosts.com, retrieved 2026-08-12), a host rig MUST be self-contained with an interior toilet and plumbed grey-water holding tank; tents, rooftop tents, and sleeping in a car/SUV/pickup are explicitly and repeatedly disallowed 'even if self-contained.' wattnap's own definition of a sleep spot is 'a place a driver sleeps in their car overnight' -- the one vehicle type both networks name-check as ineligible. RECOMMENDATION: not worth surfacing as pinned sleep spots in-app. Even setting aside the no-fabrication rule (which alone rules out plotting real host addresses without a paid account), the core offering is structurally mismatched with car-sleeping: a member who signs up would not actually be able to use most hosts in the way this app's users travel. If wattnap ever adds support for self-contained camper/van trips as a distinct mode, these networks would be worth a single informational link-out (to harvesthosts.com/discover and boondockerswelcome.com) rather than individual pins -- since real host identities can only be surfaced to paying, logged-in members, not baked into a public GeoJSON file.
